title: Cocones as an inserter and equifier
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, a category $\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets, a $\mathcal U$-small category $J$, and a diagram $D:J\to\mathcal A$. Let $\mathcal B=\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}\mathcal A$, let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be constant at $(D(j))_j$, and let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be diagonal. Let $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)$ with projection $V:\mathcal I\to\mathcal A$ as in [def-coef-inserter]. Put $\mathcal B'=\prod_{a\in\operatorname{Mor}J}\mathcal A$, let $H:\mathcal I\to\mathcal B'$ be constant at $(D(\operatorname{dom}a))_a$, and let $K:\mathcal I\to\mathcal B'$ be the diagonal of $V$. There are natural transformations $\alpha,\beta:H\Rightarrow K$ whose components at $(X,(u_j)_j)$ are $\alpha_a=u_{\operatorname{cod}a}\circ D(a)$ and $\beta_a=u_{\operatorname{dom}a}$. The full subcategory of $\mathcal I$ on objects $(X,u)$ satisfying $\alpha_{(X,u)}=\beta_{(X,u)}$ is canonically the category $\operatorname{Cocone}(D)$: its objects are pairs $(X,(u_j:D(j)\to X)_j)$ with $u_{\operatorname{cod}a}D(a)=u_{\operatorname{dom}a}$, and its morphisms are the maps commuting with all $u_j$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: explicit identification of Cocone(D) as the equifier of two transformations on the inserter of the constant and diagonal functors.

proof.text: The product category $\mathcal B=\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}\mathcal A$ has objects and arrows coordinatewise. For $X\in\mathcal A$, the constant functor has components $F(X)_j=D(j)$ and the diagonal has components $G(X)_j=X$. Therefore an object of the inserter $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)$ is exactly a pair $(X,(u_j)_j)$ with $u_j:D(j)\to X$. For two such objects, the inserter morphism condition is exactly $h\circ u_j=u\prime_j$ for every $j$, so the projection to $\mathcal A$ is the stated vertex projection $V$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product and inserter clauses; explicit description of the inserter objects and arrows.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B\prime=\prod_{a\in\operatorname{Mor}J}\mathcal A$. On an inserter object $(X,(u_j)_j)$ define $H(X,u)=(D(\operatorname{dom}a))_a$ and $K(X,u)=(X)_a$. For each arrow $a:j\to j\prime$ of $J$, set $\alpha_a=u_{j\prime}\circ D(a)$ and $\beta_a=u_j$. If $h:(X,u)\to(Y,v)$ is an inserter morphism, then $h\circ u_j=v_j$ for every $j$, so $h\circ\alpha_a=v_{j\prime}D(a)$ and $h\circ\beta_a=v_j$; hence these component maps define natural transformations $\alpha,\beta:H\Rightarrow K$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones; construction and naturality of the two transformations on the second product.

proof.text: An object $(X,u)$ lies in the equifier of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ exactly when, for every $a:j\to j\prime$, its component equality $u_{j\prime}D(a)=u_j$ holds. By the definition of a cocone, this is precisely the cocone condition for the family $(u_j:D(j)\to X)_j$. The equifier is full, so its morphisms are exactly the inserter morphisms; by the first step these are exactly the maps $h:X\to Y$ satisfying $h\circ u_j=v_j$ for all $j$. Thus the object and morphism assignments give a canonical identification with $\operatorname{Cocone}(D)$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: the equifier of the two transformations is precisely the category of cocones.

proof.text: If $J$ is empty, both products are empty products, the families $(u_j)_j$ and the equations indexed by $\operatorname{Mor}J$ are empty, and the equifier imposes no additional condition. This agrees with the category of cocones on the empty diagram: an object is just an object of $\mathcal A$ with its unique empty family of legs, and a morphism is any map in $\mathcal A$. Hence the identification also covers the empty diagram.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: explicit cocone identification, including the empty diagram.

proof_origin.place: Explicit expansion of the categorical cocone identification used in the proof paragraph on accessible cocones.
